 Mitchell Robinson delivered 12 points (6-of-6 FGs, 0-of-2 FTs), seven rebounds, two assists, four steals and one block over 18 minutes off the bench in Sunday’s win over the Bucks. 
 It was encouraging to see Robinson deliver an impactful performance on both ends of the floor off the bench after entering the contest questionable due to illness. The 28-year-old big man continues to take a back seat to Neemias Queta, who had 13 points and nine rebounds in 22 minutes in this one, but it hasn’t prevented him from remaining a force on the glass.

 Mitchell Robinson (illness) is questionable for Sunday’s game against the Bucks. 
 Robinson’s late addition to the Celtics’ injury report isn’t a good sign. If he can’t play, Neemias Queta and Luka Garza should see more minutes. 
 Neemias Queta 
 BOS 
 Center 
 #88 
 Neemias Queta produced nine points (4-of-8 FGs, 1-of-3 FTs), 12 rebounds, three assists and two blocks in Wednesday’s win over the Bucks. 
 Queta remained in the Celtics’ starting lineup on Wednesday, logging 29 minutes and grabbing 12 rebounds. Mitchell Robinson (3/10/1/1/1), who began the season as the starting center, played 20 minutes, while Luka Garza (11/5/2/1 with three three-pointers) logged 18 minutes. Queta should be rostered in standard leagues, especially if he continues to start. However, the Celtics going three-deep at center does the trio no favors for fantasy value. 
 Neemias Queta

 #88 
 Neemias Queta recorded 16 points (6-of-7 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), six rebounds, one assist and one three-pointer in Monday’s loss to the Rockets. 
 Despite Mitchell Robinson being available after sitting out Sunday’s win over the Magic, Celtics head coach Joe Mazzulla stuck with Queta as his starting center. The points, rebounds and percentages were good, but those rostering Queta likely hoped to get some defensive production as well. Queta played 26 minutes to Robinson’s 15, a promising development for those rostering the former if that minutes split holds. 
 Luka Garza

 Center 
 #52 
 Luka Garza produced 14 points (4-of-9 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), three rebounds, one block and four three-pointers in Monday’s loss to the Rockets. 
 While Mitchell Robinson (four points, four rebounds) was available for Monday’s game, Garza played 18 minutes after logging 21 in Sunday’s win over the Magic. The Celtics’ third center established new season highs in points and three-pointers. Garza isn’t where he should be in redraft leagues, but that could change down the line, given Robinson’s injury history.

 Mitchell Robinson (rest) did not play in the first game of Boston’s road back-to-back, so Queta started at center. While he didn’t offer much scoring, the 7-footer was effective on the glass and as a rim protector. On offense, the Celtics got solid contributions from Luka Garza, who finished with 10 points, two rebounds, one assist, and two three-pointers. Boston visits Houston on Monday, and Robinson should return to the starting lineup.

 Jeremiah Fears recorded 25 points (10-of-14 FGs, 2-of-4 FTs), six rebounds, five assists, two steals and three three-pointers in Sunday’s loss to the Clippers.
 Fears continues to spread his wings as the Pelicans’ point guard, scoring at least 19 points in three straight games and in five of his last six appearances. What’s especially encouraging for those rostering the second-year guard is that the return of Dejounte Murray (6/3/3 in 28 minutes) has not led to a decrease in production. Fears’ current fantasy value sits just outside the top-100, but that will change if he continues to play as he has over the last week.

 Trey Murphy accounted for 26 points (9-of-17 FGs, 4-of-4 FTs), seven rebounds, three assists, one steal and four three-pointers in Sunday’s loss to the Clippers.
 After shooting 12-of-28 from the field in his prior three appearances, Murphy made over 50 percent of his shots on Sunday. Add in the rebounds, assists and three-pointers, and this was a good finish to Week 3 for the Pelicans forward. The 26 points matched Murphy’s season high, and he’ll look to build on this effort when the Pelicans begin a four-game Week 4 on Monday against the Warriors.

 Zion Williamson finished Sunday’s loss to the Clippers with 25 points (9-of-9 FGs, 7-of-9 FTs), four rebounds and two assists.
 Williamson produced excellent percentages in his final game of the week, much to the delight of those rostering him in category leagues. Unfortunately, the production outside of the points and percentages was pretty lean in the Pelicans’ 139-123 defeat. That said, over three weeks, Williamson’s production has exceeded his ADP (69) by a safe distance. The hope is that he can avoid the extended absence that has been a common occurrence throughout his NBA career.
